Where it began

Saim Ayub was born in Karachi on 24 May 2002. He came to the game young, through tape-ball cricket in Gulistan-e-Johar.

His senior career moved fast. He played his first Twenty20 match for Quetta Gladiators in the Pakistan Super League in February 2021, his first List A game for Sindh in March 2022, and his first first-class match, also for Sindh, that September. In the 2023 Super League, batting for Peshawar Zalmi, he hit 74 from 34 balls in one game and made 341 runs for the season at a strike rate of 165.53.

The player

He is a left-handed batter who also bowls off-spin. Pakistan first brought him into a Test squad in December 2022, mainly so that he could learn the ropes, and he made his Test debut at Sydney on 3 January 2024. Against England at Multan in October 2024 he made 77, his highest Test score. By November 2026 he had played 9 Tests, scoring 364 runs with three fifties and taking 4 wickets.

The white-ball game is where he made his biggest early mark. In Zimbabwe late in 2024 he reached an ODI hundred from 53 balls, the second-fastest by a Pakistani, and was player of the series. On the tour of South Africa that followed he made back-to-back ODI hundreds, the second of them a match-winning 101 that completed Pakistan's first ODI clean sweep there. An injury cut that tour short, but he was back in the side by August 2025.

What made him special

His trademark is the no-look shot: he swings the ball away towards the leg side while turning his eyes elsewhere, as if the outcome were no concern of his. He first tried it on the spur of the moment in a domestic T20 game in 2022, and has since hit no-look sixes in both the Super League and first-class cricket.

His Test batting average of 22.75 shows that, by late 2026, Test runs had come a little less freely than white-ball ones. His bowling, meanwhile, grew into a real asset: after the 2025 Asia Cup he rose to the top of the ICC rankings for T20I all-rounders.

Further afield

He has travelled widely in franchise cricket, with spells for Rangpur Riders and Durdanto Dhaka in Bangladesh and Guyana Amazon Warriors in the Caribbean. In the 2026 Super League he joined Hyderabad Kingsmen.

And finally

In the 2023 Super League, one of his rapid half-centuries had observers comparing him with Saeed Anwar, which is heady company for a batter barely out of his teens. As for the no-look shot, it breaks the very first rule every young cricketer is taught, which may be exactly why crowds love it.
